title: marketplace-catalog-friction-mitigation-and-copy-experiments
content:
Context and goal:
This is a working playbook for reducing friction in partner catalog listing flows (tile acceptance, trial provisioning, and demo conversion). Focus: practical gates + lightweight copy experiments that can be iterated quickly with the storefront engineering team.

Background:
- We keep seeing 3 predictable drop points in partner listings: (1) eligibility checks on tile submission, (2) trial/entitlement provisioning failures, (3) low CTR on listing tiles due to unclear value props.
- Aim: build a small, reproducible checklist + 6 copy variants for A/B testing, and define minimal telemetry to detect regressions early.

Scope (what this doc contains):
- Acceptance gating checklist (technical + legal + UX) for partner listing approval
- Lightweight copy variants for hero and feature bullets (6 variants)
- Demo/test scenarios + smoke tests for provisioning and entitlement flows
- Telemetry events to surface in the Console and Product Analytics
- Quick remediation runbook for common failure modes

Acceptance gating checklist (tiered):
1) Basic metadata and assets (automated checks)
   - tile name, short description (<=140 chars), long description (optional) present
   - logo PNG (square 400x400) uploaded, alt text provided
   - primary CTA defined (Try / Contact Sales / Docs)
   - scoped tags: model-type, use-case, industry (3 max)
   - automated asset-scan passes (no prohibited content)

2) Functional/technical checks (manual + automated)
   - API contract present and validated: sample request/response, auth method (API key/OAuth)
   - Trial provisioning flow smoke test (see test matrix below) green
   - Billing/entitlement mapping: SKU defined and linked to provisioned capacity
   - Region compatibility note (US/EU/APAC): declared and tested

3) Security & legal (requires review signoff)
   - Data handling statement (no storage of customer PII unless declared)
   - Compliance flags: SOC2, ISO, HIPAA (if claimed) — attach proof or disable claim
   - Export control / restricted model usage checklist reviewed

4) UX & copy (product reviewer)
   - Short description is customer-facing, no marketing hyperbole, one-sentence outcome
   - Hero/feature bullets pair with icons and are scannable (<=12 words each)
   - Screenshot/short demo video attached where possible

Quick checklist for listing reviewer (one-line):
- Metadata OK, assets OK, API & trial smoke green, legal flags resolved, copy reviewed, telemetry hooks in place.

Copy experiments (6 hero variants) — short (single-sentence) lines for tile hero area. Keep under 120 chars.
Variant A (Outcome-first): "Fast, cost-predictable LLM inference for production apps — deploy in minutes, scale reliably."
Variant B (Developer-first): "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and clear unit economics — SDKs + rollout tools included."
Variant C (Security): "Private deployments & VPC-ready runtime with audit logs and KMS integrations."
Variant D (Performance): "Sub-100ms p99 token latency at scale — optimized kernels and caching out-of-the-box."
Variant E (Value/Price): "Cut inference unit costs with smart batching and quantization recommendations."
Variant F (Hybrid): "Hosted API today, private deployments later — same API, same telemetry."

Feature bullet pairs (short headline — 8–12 words; sub-bullet explanatory phrase) — pick 3 per tile:
- "Predictable latency" — "Autoscaling and routing policies ensure consistent p99 across traffic spikes."
- "Cost controls" — "Intelligent batching, caching, and quantization suggestions that lower USD/token."
- "Private-ready" — "VPC and on‑prem deployment options with KMS support and audit trails."
- "Observability" — "Per-route tracing, token-level cost breakdowns, and regression alerts."
- "Rollouts and safety" — "Canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic safe fallbacks to lower-capacity models."
- "Model catalog" — "Curated open models with Redwood-verified performance profiles and version pinning."

CTA variants to test (3):
- Primary: "Start free trial"
- Secondary: "Request a demo"
- Tertiary: "View docs"

Demo and smoke test scenarios (automation first):
1) New partner listing basic smoke
   - Create listing, upload logo, add metadata, tick privacy checkboxes
   - Expected: Listing saved, preview renders; backend returns 200.
2) Trial provisioning happy path
   - Trigger trial provisioning via API (test SKU); emulate metered response
   - Expected: Entitlement created, trial tokens in console, email notification (mock)
3) Trial provisioning partial failure
   - Simulate quota allocation failure (quota service returns 503)
   - Expected: Retry policy triggers, onboarding email has clear troubleshooting steps, partner tile marked 'provisioning delayed' in UI
4) Region mismatch rejection
   - Claim region APAC but provisioning only US
   - Expected: Listing flagged, reviewer notified, tile blocked from public catalog until remediated
5) Metrics/usage ingestion
   - Generate 100 sample calls (diverse sequence lengths); verify token-level telemetry and p99 latency recorded

Minimal telemetry events to require before publish (these feed Console + Pager/Slack triggers):
- listing.created (listing_id, owner_id, tags)
- listing.preview_rendered (listing_id, asset_checks_passed:true/false)
- provisioning.started (listing_id, sku, region)
- provisioning.succeeded (listing_id, sku, capacity_allocated)
- provisioning.failed (listing_id, error_code, retry_count)
- trial.consumption (org_id, tokens_consumed, p95_latency)
- listing.legal_flagged (listing_id, flag_type)
Quick queries for PM/RevOps on day-1 after publish:
- #failed_provisionings by partner in last 24h
- average onboarding time (created -> provisioning.succeeded)
- CTR by hero variant (A-F) and CTA variant (Start free trial / Request demo / View docs)

Failure-mode remediation runbook (short):
- provisioning.failed with transient 5xx: schedule exponential retry (3 attempts), push notification to partner success + mark tile as 'provisioning delayed' visible in console
- provisioning.failed with 403 (quota/permissions): auto-open issue in Jira-PL queue with owner tag + email partner contact template (see linked_artifacts)
- listing.legal_flagged: move tile to private review and block publish until legal sign-off; escalate to Legal lead if >48h

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we require video demo for all enterprise-tier partners? (ops cost tradeoff)
- Standardized screenshot size and whether we allow animated GIFs in tile assets
- Exact SLA for provisioning success time (TBD: 30m vs 2h for reserved capacity)

Next steps (owner: Ava)
- [ ] Align with storefront eng on minimal telemetry contract (deadline: 2025-01-20)
- [ ] Run copy A/B with 5 internal beta partners (deadline: 2025-02-07)
- [ ] Create automation jobs for smoke tests 1–4 and wire to PR pipeline (assign Marco)
- [ ] Draft partner-facing troubleshooting email templates (assign Samantha)

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive and low-friction — aim to unblock listings quickly while retaining safety.
- Keep copy variants short; we'll iterate based on CTR and onboarding time.
- Attach test PRs and telemetry schema to the linked artifacts when ready.

Example lightweight partner-facing description (for tile long description / partner portal):
"Redwood Inference provides a unified inference runtime that delivers predictable latency, cost-aware controls, and private deployment options. Use our hosted API to get started quickly and move to dedicated or VPC deployments as you scale. Includes per-route observability, canary rollouts, and automated batching recommendations to reduce unit costs."
